tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Start with get_started. Choose a local deployment or a provisioned remote host, then attach or launch, inspect capabilities, debug, and detach safely. Stepping and call tracing are best-effort and cannot expose optimized, native, runtime, or missing-sequence-point calls. Summarize Gateway, deployment, and host state and recommend the next safe action. Names the Gateway's own build, which is where these tool descriptions and response shapes come from, and flags skew against the debugger host builds. Quote gateway_build and build_skew in anything reported about tool behaviour.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Run bounded read-only diagnostics for Gateway state, deployment roots, host registry, ports, and registered debugger hosts. Includes a build_skew check that fails when the Gateway and a host come from different commits, or when dgSpy was reinstalled after this Gateway process started.

tools.name: get_workflow_help
tools.description: Return one focused workflow from the same authoritative grouping exposed at dgspy://guide/workflows. Each result includes concise guidance and exact recommended tool names.

tools.name: get_local_deployment
tools.description: Report the active and previous managed local deployment.

tools.name: launch_local_host
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING. Ensure exactly one managed local host is running: adopt one that is already running the installed payload, install and launch when none is, and never start a second process beside a running one. Fails with host_already_running when a different build owns the endpoint; replace=true then detaches that host's targets, closes it, and launches the installed payload, which ends its debugging sessions. Pass elevated=true when a target process is missing from list_programs because it belongs to another user or to a service; the result reports the host's actual elevation.

replace.description: Close a running host that is not the installed payload and launch that payload instead. Detaches its targets first; any debugging session it holds ends.

allow_terminate.description: With replace, proceed even when a target cannot be detached without killing it. Destroys that process.

elevated.description: Launch the host elevated, so it can see and attach to processes owned by other users and by services. Prompts for User Account Control on the interactive desktop; a dismissed prompt fails with elevation_declined. A running host is adopted only when it is already elevated. Requires the default state root and no DGSPY_HOST_ID, DGSPY_RPC_TOKEN or DGSPY_RPC_PORT override, because elevation cannot pass them to the host.

tools.name: rollback_local_deployment
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING. Atomically switch current back to the retained previous version.

tools.name: uninstall_local_deployment
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE and audited. Remove managed program versions after explicit confirmation; settings are preserved unless remove_settings is true.

tools.name: create_remote_host_package
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Personalize the bundled self-contained host payload and create a remote ZIP; it never builds, transfers, or executes the host. compression defaults to optimal; use none for fastest extraction or fastest for light compression.

tools.name: get_remote_host_readiness
tools.description: Report registry and live connection readiness for a remote host.

tools.name: revoke_remote_host
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE and audited. Remove a remote host from the central registry after explicit confirmation.

tools.name: step_and_inspect
tools.description: Step once, wait for the resulting stop, and return the new location, compact stack, frame, watches, and exception in one bounded workflow.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: trace_calls
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Perform bounded best-effort managed step-into tracing. Optimized, native, runtime, async, and missing-sequence-point calls can be unobservable.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: run_to_method
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. The composed way to reach or arrive at a method through the target's natural control flow: set a temporary method breakpoint, continue, wait boundedly, and always remove the temporary breakpoint. It does not invoke the method or make unreachable code execute. Read wait.timed_out: true means no arrival, the temporary breakpoint is gone, and the target is running again.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

module.description: Legacy name/path selector; module_id is exact and preferred.

tools.name: run_to_location
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. The composed way to reach or arrive at an IL location through the target's natural control flow: set a temporary IL breakpoint, continue, wait boundedly, and always remove the temporary breakpoint. It does not invoke code or make an unreachable location execute. Read wait.timed_out: true means no arrival, the temporary breakpoint is gone, and the target is running again.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

module.description: Legacy name/path selector; module_id is exact and preferred.

tools.name: run_atomic_action
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Versioned bounded natural-arrival workflow with an owned internal breakpoint, explicit action and verification, ownership-scoped cleanup, and independent action/interruption/cleanup outcomes. operation_version and request schema_version are currently 1. Initial action kinds are capture, assignment, and method_invocation; managed_payload arrives later through the same IAtomicAction extension point. Capture and assignment accept only addressable dotted paths; values and invocation arguments are JSON scalars, so this is not an open-ended expression program.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

serialized_value.description: A JSON null, boolean, number, or string.

items.description: A JSON null, boolean, number, or string.

request.description: Atomic action request schema v1: action_id, action_name, process_id, runtime_id, app_domain_id, module_id from discovery (preferred; module is legacy), method_token, il_offset, optional nearby_offsets, deadline_utc, resume_policy and disconnect_policy.

tools.name: initialize_hooklab
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING. Initialize HookLab in the selected process. dgSpy pauses only as needed, selects an evaluable managed thread, injects the resident runtime, verifies its control channel, and restores the process's prior running state.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: get_hooklab_status
tools.description: Report whether HookLab is initialized and ready in a process.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_hook_template
tools.description: Generate editable no-op Prefix, Postfix, or paired Prefix/Postfix C# source for one exactly selected non-generic method. Read-only: resolves metadata only and does not initialize HookLab or modify the target.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

tools.name: install_hook
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Install an observation hook, or create/update compiled custom Prefix/Postfix source when source and a monotonically increasing revision are supplied. Exact MVID, token, signature, and IL digest guards are required. Prototype custom hooks use the same-user unauthenticated resident pipe.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

source.description: Complete C# source declaring one public static method matching kind and optionally its Prefix/Postfix companion.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: list_hooks
tools.description: List HookLab observation hooks owned by this dgSpy session.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_hook_events
tools.description: Read bounded HookLab events after a cursor through the resident control channel while the target keeps running.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: remove_hook
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Remove one HookLab-owned Harmony patch by hook_id through the resident control channel.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: remove_all_hooks
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Remove every HookLab-owned Harmony patch in one process through the resident control channel.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: start_atomic_action
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Start the same bounded natural-arrival workflow as run_atomic_action, but return as soon as the action is REGISTERED - before lease acquisition and before breakpoint binding - so the caller's single host connection stays free to poll status or cancel. Answers accepted, action_id, phase and recommended_poll_after_ms. Prefer this over run_atomic_action: a blocking run occupies the one channel for its whole budget, so nothing can reach the action while it runs. Poll get_atomic_action_status at the interval it recommends; there is deliberately no wait operation, because a wait would block the channel again. disconnect_policy is not accepted here - after acceptance the action is host-owned and ends only on its deadline or an explicit cancel_atomic_action.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

serialized_value.description: A JSON null, boolean, number, or string.

items.description: A JSON null, boolean, number, or string.

request.description: Atomic action request schema v1: action_id, action_name, process_id, runtime_id, app_domain_id, module_id from discovery (preferred; module is legacy), method_token, il_offset, optional nearby_offsets, deadline_utc and resume_policy. disconnect_policy is rejected on this operation.

tools.name: get_atomic_action_status
tools.description: Read a versioned terminal or in-progress atomic-action record by action_id. Reports phase (queued, arming, armed, running, executing, verifying, cleaning_up, terminal - monotonic), completed, cancel_requested, recommended_poll_after_ms, and the terminal result once there is one. This is also the reconciliation operation named after an ambiguous cleanup or potentially side-effecting outcome, including after the debug session ended.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: cancel_atomic_action
tools.description: Request cancellation of a bounded atomic action. Accepted in every non-terminal phase, including queued and arming. Cancellation runs the same ownership-scoped cleanup path and does not discard the terminal status record. Authorized by the record's captured session and process generation plus the exact action_id - it deliberately takes no expected_execution_version, because that counter was measured not to move during an action and a caller could never hold a fresh one in time to cancel. A terminal action answers cancel_requested=false with completed=true; an unknown id or an older generation answers action_not_found.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description: List registered debugger hosts and their current connection state.

tools.name: get_host_info
tools.description: Identify the dnSpy host this gateway talks to: versions, machine, architecture, supported engines, and whether a session is live.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Report what this host supports before relying on it: per-operation time bounds, per-engine behavior (notably that Mono/Unity binds breakpoints only at sequence points), limits, and the complete event_kinds and stop_reasons vocabularies. Engine differences are advertised here rather than assumed.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_programs
tools.description: List dnSpy-attachable managed runtimes. Unfiltered enumeration probes every process on the machine and takes seconds; pass process_ids or process_names when the target is known. Each call replaces the set of valid program_id values.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

process_names.description: Process names, wildcards * and ? allowed, eg. UltimateChickenHorse*.

provider_names.description: dnSpy attach providers to consult: DotNetFramework, DotNet, UnityEditor, UnityPlayer. Naming providers skips the rest. UnityPlayer runs a multicast scan and is skipped entirely unless named.

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Attach using a program_id returned by list_programs. When the user supplies a PID, call list_programs with process_ids:[PID] first, then attach the exact returned runtime.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: attach_endpoint
tools.description: Attach to a Mono/Unity soft-debugger endpoint by address and port. Use this when the target was launched with --debugger-agent=transport=dt_socket,server=y,address=HOST:PORT: such a target emits no discovery beacon, so list_programs can never see it and attach cannot reach it. Returns state "faulted" with fault_message when the connection fails. A server=y agent accepts EXACTLY ONE connection per launch, so never TCP-probe the port to check whether the target is up: the probe consumes the single connection permanently, and this tool then faults with a connection error that reads like a target-side problem when the target is fine. Connect only with this tool, once. A clean detach makes the agent listen again; anything else means relaunching the target.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

engine.description: Default unity. Must match the target's runtime.

process_is_suspended.description: True when the agent was given suspend=y, ie. the target is parked waiting for a debugger.

connection_timeout_ms.description: Socket retry window. dnSpy's default is 10000; capped at 300000.

tools.name: launch
tools.description: Launch a target through dnSpy's debugger engine. Unlike attach, dnSpy owns the process, so terminate and restart have deterministic semantics, and the target's stdout/stderr can be captured — get_output carries them. When break_at is create_process or entry_point, the reply waits for that initial stop and its returned state/versions describe the stopped process. This call creates the process before its wait completes, so its side effect outlives a cancelled call: if it is interrupted ("Tool execution was interrupted"), assume the process EXISTS and do not treat that as failure. Retrying is safe — a repeat launch of the same image adopts the live session it already started instead of creating a second debuggee, and returns that session — but list_sessions shows it too, under a program_id of "launch:<engine>:<path>".

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

redirect_output.description: Default true: capture the target's stdout/stderr and publish them to get_output and wait_for_output. False gives the target its own console, whose output nothing can read back.

adopt_existing.description: Default true: when a live launch session already owns this image, return it instead of starting a second process. This is what makes an interrupted launch safe to retry. Pass false only to run a second copy of the same program deliberately.

tools.name: get_session_state
tools.description: Get current debugger session state. You rarely need this before a mutation: every attach, launch, wait and guarded call returns the same counters in a `versions` object (lifecycle_version, execution_version, breakpoints_version, stop_id, last_event_id), read after that call applied. Take the next call's `expected_*` guards from there and call this only to resynchronize after an error or after something outside this client moved the target. Guards and cursors are different kinds of number — guards are versions, cursors are event ids, and one is never accepted for the other. `versions.last_event_id` is the newest event AT RESPONSE TIME, so it is a correct cursor for reading history with get_events, and the WRONG one to wait from for an event the same call is about to cause: a breakpoint on a hot path can be hit before a resume even returns, and waiting from a cursor that already includes that stop waits for the next one. To wait for a stop, use a cursor captured BEFORE the resume — set_breakpoint and set_il_breakpoint return exactly that as `cursor_event_id`.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List active debugger sessions. Use this to recover a session_id.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_session_controller
tools.description: Report whether a debugger session currently has an MCP controller. Inspection never claims it or changes target state. When owned, controller_expires_utc and controller_expires_in_seconds say when the lease lapses if that controller never calls again, so a caller that legitimately lost its transport — the MCP client replacing its stdio server gives the session a new identity and strands the old lease on a dead one — can wait a known interval instead of polling blind, then claim_session. controller_is_caller distinguishes "someone else holds it" from "you already do".

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: claim_session
tools.description: Explicitly claim an unowned or expired debugger session after caller or Gateway recovery. A live owner is refused with session_owned so the operator can be warned; after that warning, force=true intentionally transfers control without changing target state.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

force.description: Default false. Set true only after inspecting the current controller and warning its operator; transfers the controller lease but does not resume, pause, or detach the target.

tools.name: release_session
tools.description: Release controller ownership without resuming, detaching, terminating, or otherwise changing the target.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: detach
tools.description: Detach one selected process or all targets. Fails with detach_would_terminate unless allow_terminate is explicit. If the engine does not actually remove the target within 10 seconds, returns detach_timed_out and preserves the session instead of claiming success.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

allow_terminate.description: Stop debugging even if that terminates the selected target.

expected_lifecycle_version.description: Required exact lifecycle_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: terminate
tools.description: Terminate one selected process or every active target explicitly.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_lifecycle_version.description: Required exact lifecycle_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Restart a target previously launched through dgSpy. Attached targets cannot be restarted because dgSpy does not own their launch options.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_lifecycle_version.description: Required exact lifecycle_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: pause
tools.description: Pause one process. process_id is optional only when exactly one process is active.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: continue
tools.description: Continue one process. process_id is optional only when exactly one process is active. It does not wait for the next stop. Capture the wait cursor BEFORE calling this — set_breakpoint returns one as cursor_event_id — because a breakpoint on a hot path can be hit before this call returns, and `versions.last_event_id` in the response would then already include that stop, so waiting from it waits for the one after. To resume as far as a known place instead, run_to_method and run_to_location do the breakpoint/continue/wait/cleanup round in one call.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: set_il_breakpoint
tools.description: Set an exact module/token/IL-offset breakpoint and report whether the engine actually bound it. Check `bound`: false with severity "error" will never be hit, false with no error is pending a module load. On Mono/Unity a breakpoint can only sit on a sequence point; many offsets qualify but a frame's own il_offset often does not. By default, when the engine refuses the requested offset, dgSpy snaps to the first legal sequence point at or after it; only when no later point exists does it use the method's final preceding sequence point. `snapped`, `requested_il_offset`, and `il_offset` report exactly what happened. Pass snap_to_sequence_point=false to keep the refusal instead. Pass the returned `cursor_event_id` to wait_for_stop as after_event_id: a cursor read after this call has already missed the first hit on a hot method. The breakpoint starts unconditional — attach a condition, hit count or trace message by passing the returned breakpoint_id to update_breakpoint. Use get_il to see which offsets are sequence points before choosing one.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

module.description: Legacy name/path selector; module_id is exact and preferred.

snap_to_sequence_point.description: Default true. On refusal, use the first legal sequence point at or after the requested offset; when none exists, use the method's final preceding sequence point.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: list_breakpoints
tools.description: List all dnSpy breakpoints with their binding state. Breakpoints are global and outlive a session. engine_hit_count reports times the engine reached each breakpoint this session, counted before conditions run — a false-but-working condition still ticks it, distinguishing 'condition not yet true' from 'never reached'.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: remove_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove one breakpoint by the exact id returned by set_il_breakpoint or list_breakpoints. Unlike clear_breakpoints, this leaves every other dnSpy and UI breakpoint untouched.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: clear_breakpoints
tools.description: Remove every dnSpy breakpoint, including any set by hand in the dnSpy UI. Breakpoints outlive a detach and rebind on the next attach, so clear them before reattaching if a fresh session should not stop on old ones. To drop only your own, remove_breakpoint takes one id and leaves the rest alone; to be able to put a human's back, export_breakpoints first and import_breakpoints after.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: wait_for_stop
tools.description: Wait without polling for stops after an event cursor. Concurrent waiters do not consume events. THE CURSOR IS YOURS TO TRACK: because reads are non-destructive the server keeps no per-caller position, so every response carries last_event_id and you pass it as the next call's after_event_id. Omitting after_event_id means "from the start of the session", NOT "only what is new": a bare call replays every retained stop, so a poll loop that never advances it re-processes stops it already handled. That default is deliberate — the opposite one would silently drop a stop that landed between two calls, and a duplicate is recoverable where a lost stop is not. Seed the first cursor from set_il_breakpoint's cursor_event_id or attach's last_event_id rather than reading one afterwards. A truncated result supplies oldest_available_cursor so the caller can recover. A cursor beyond the newest event is rejected with cursor_ahead_of_stream instead of waiting forever — cursors come from cursor_event_id, event_id, or last_event_id, never from a version counter.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

after_event_id.description: Exclusive cursor: return only events with a higher id. Pass the previous response's last_event_id, or set_il_breakpoint's cursor_event_id. Default 0 replays the whole retained session.

timeout_ms.description: Default 5000. The extension clamps to 10000; poll again with the returned cursor for longer waits.

tools.name: wait_for_event
tools.description: Wait without polling for any requested event kinds after a cursor. Returns immediately when a matching buffered event already exists; concurrent waiters are non-destructive. The cursor is caller-supplied on exactly the terms described on wait_for_stop: advance after_event_id with each response's last_event_id, and note that omitting it replays the session's retained history rather than returning only new events. A cursor beyond the newest event is rejected with cursor_ahead_of_stream instead of waiting forever.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

after_event_id.description: Exclusive cursor: return only events with a higher id. Pass the previous response's last_event_id, or set_il_breakpoint's cursor_event_id. Default 0 replays the whole retained session.

kinds.description: Optional normalized event-kind filter. An unrecognized kind is rejected with invalid_argument rather than silently matching nothing.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Read the STRUCTURED stream: normalized lifecycle and debugger events, without consuming them. Nothing the target printed appears here — console text is get_output. Optional kinds filter the bounded per-session stream; truncated reports when the requested cursor is older than retained history, and a cursor beyond the newest event is rejected with cursor_ahead_of_stream rather than returning a clean empty result. Shares one bounded buffer and one caller-supplied cursor with wait_for_stop and wait_for_event: advance after_event_id with each response's last_event_id, since omitting it returns the retained history rather than only what is new.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

after_event_id.description: Exclusive cursor: return only events with a higher id. Pass the previous response's last_event_id. Default 0 returns the whole retained session.

kinds.description: Optional normalized event-kind filter. An unrecognized kind is rejected with invalid_argument rather than silently matching nothing.

tools.name: get_stop_reason
tools.description: Read the latest normalized stop, or an exact retained stop event by event_id, including process, thread, breakpoint, exception, and location details when supplied by the debugger. stop_reason is one of: breakpoint, exception, step, entry_point, program_break, pause, unknown.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: List paused target threads with stable thread_id values. It does not eagerly fetch every stack because Unity threads can exit during frame retrieval; select a returned thread_id with get_callstack or get_frame. Do not try to predict func-eval viability from `states`: CorDebug publishes UnsafePoint there and Mono publishes no equivalent at all, so a rule learned on one engine is wrong on the other. Pass include_evaluability instead. A blocked result carries recovery at the point of decision: use the composed run_to_method or run_to_location workflow rather than manually assembling breakpoint, continue, wait, and cleanup. Those workflows wait for reachable code; they do not make an otherwise unreachable method execute. If arrival needs an external stimulus, issue the run-to call first and drive the stimulus while it waits.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

include_evaluability.description: Default false. True probes each thread and adds can_evaluate, evaluate_blocked_reason (no_frames, native_frame, or unsafe_point), and recovery when blocked. Follow that recovery directly; it names the composed run-to workflow. Costs one bounded stack walk per thread; on Unity that is the call a disappearing thread can stall, which is why it is opt-in.

tools.name: get_callstack
tools.description: Get a paused call stack and primitive locals. Pass thread_id for deterministic caller-selected inspection; omitting it preserves the managed-frame probe fallback. Expression compilation uses the selected frame's module context: choose the nearest managed frame whose module/module_name is the target assembly, then pass its thread_id and frame_index to evaluation tools. A fully qualified target type still cannot resolve from an unrelated module such as a Thread.Sleep frame. A frame with raw_locals true reports its locals as the runtime's raw slots V_0, V_1, ... because the engine recovered no source-level names for it; see get_frame.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_frame
tools.description: Inspect one paused frame by caller-selected thread_id and zero-based frame_index. `locals` holds primitive scalars only; pass include to also get objects and `this` in `values`, which is one round trip against one evaluation context. Values carry `address`/`address_length` when the runtime has one — see read_memory. When raw_locals is true the engine could not recover source-level variable names for this frame, so the locals are its raw slots named V_0, V_1, ...; those are ordinary expressions and can be evaluated, expanded and assigned to like any name.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

include.description: locals covers arguments too — dnSpy does not separate them. Unknown values are rejected rather than ignored.

tools.name: update_breakpoint
tools.description: THIS IS WHERE CONDITIONAL BREAKPOINTS LIVE. Change an existing breakpoint's enabled state, condition, hit count, or trace message, using a breakpoint_id from set_breakpoint, set_il_breakpoint or list_breakpoints. A condition (`i == 3`, `name == "x"`) or a hit count is how you stop at one specific loop iteration; stepping to it, or computing which iteration it would be, is neither necessary nor reliable. Conditions and hit counts are evaluated by the engine inside the target, so a condition that cannot be evaluated fails at hit time rather than here — list_breakpoints reports engine_hit_count, counted before the condition runs, which separates "condition never true" from "never reached". Pass an empty string for condition or trace_message to clear it; omit a field to leave it unchanged.

condition.description: Expression in the target's language. Empty string clears the condition.

trace_message.description: Print instead of (or as well as) stopping. Empty string clears. The message goes to dnSpy's Output window only: it is NOT on the get_output stream and produces no event, so an MCP caller cannot read it. Use a condition and a real stop instead unless a human is watching the window.

Exception breakpoints and exception policies are ONE thing: this writes the same entry set_exception_policy writes (that tool additionally takes module conditions); list with either list tool and remove with remove_exception_policy.

Bounded, with total and truncated. Same underlying entries as list_exception_policies; that tool is the raw view with module conditions, and takes the same category and name filters.

See step_and_inspect to combine a step with evaluation in one call.

Remove it first when the point is to reach the frame above.

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate an expression against a paused frame. Returns the raw scalar and dnSpy's formatted display text as separate fields, so numbers stay comparable without parsing display text. has_raw_value distinguishes a value of null from a value that is unavailable or optimized away. Running target code is guarded by TWO independent gates, both off by default and NOT interchangeable: allow_func_eval permits executing target code at all, allow_side_effects permits an expression dnSpy classifies as side-effecting. A property getter such as DateTime.Now.Ticks trips only the first, so allow_func_eval alone runs it — and it can deadlock a target holding a lock or mutate what you were inspecting, which is why it is off. An explicit method call such as Telemetry.ComputeReading(5) trips BOTH, and side effects are checked first, so passing allow_func_eval alone leaves the error "This expression causes side effects and will not be evaluated" completely unchanged, which reads like the flag was ignored and is not. Pass both for a method call, or use invoke_method, which sets both and audits the call. One exception explains conflicting reports of this tool: dnSpy's `ac` ("always calculate") format specifier, appended as `Some.Method(1), ac`, opens the side-effects gate on its own, so that shape DOES succeed with allow_func_eval alone; it is dnSpy syntax rather than a dgSpy argument and bypasses the opt-in, so prefer allow_side_effects. Every refusal carries `recovery` naming the gate that blocked it; never fall back to computing a method's result by hand. For an object, get_members expands it a level rather than guessing member names; get_autos returns what the current statement touches without naming anything; add_watch re-evaluates the same expression at every later stop, which a value read here cannot survive. A value carries `address`/`address_length` when the runtime has one, which is the supported way to reach a managed object with read_memory and write_memory. Expressions compile in the selected frame's module context. After CS0103, use get_callstack and select the nearest managed frame in the target module with thread_id and frame_index; even a fully qualified target type cannot resolve from an unrelated module. The error also names variables this frame can address, including V_n slots when it reports no source-level names.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

thread_id.description: Defaults to the thread that carried the stop.

allow_func_eval.description: Default false. True permits running target code, eg. property getters and ToString. It does NOT imply allow_side_effects and cannot substitute for it.

allow_side_effects.description: Default false. True permits an expression dnSpy classifies as side-effecting, which every explicit method call is. Required in addition to allow_func_eval to call a method, including a pure one — dnSpy classifies by expression shape, not by what the method actually does.

tools.name: invoke_method
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Evaluate a complete method-call expression in the paused target. This injects a nested func-eval; it is not natural-control-flow arrival at the method, and breakpoints inside the invoked call are not serviced. Never use it to satisfy a request to reach or arrive at code: use run_to_method or run_to_location, whose timed_out result proves whether natural execution arrived. Func-eval and side effects are always enabled by this tool boundary and cannot be downgraded or enabled accidentally through evaluate. On failure read compiler_error: true means the expression never compiled and nothing ran, so fix the expression; false means it compiled and the engine refused to execute it here, so the same call can succeed against another thread or another stop. A func-eval needs a thread the engine will let it start on — call list_threads with include_evaluability=true and pass a thread_id whose can_evaluate is true. If none qualifies, prepare or drive the target state, then use run_to_method or run_to_location to reach a managed frame that can evaluate. For CS0103, use get_callstack and select the nearest frame in the target module; qualification alone does not make a type visible from an unrelated frame module.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: create_object
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Evaluate a complete object-construction expression in the paused target. Func-eval and side effects are always enabled. compiler_error and thread selection work exactly as described on invoke_method.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description: Read up to 65536 bytes from the selected debug process. Returns base64 and the runtime capability used. To get the address of a managed object, read the `address` and `address_length` fields that evaluate, get_members and get_frame report for every value that has one — for a string or an array that is the element data, so it is what you want for the bytes. Do NOT reach for GCHandle.Alloc(x, Pinned).AddrOfPinnedObject() through invoke_method: it costs a func-eval and leaks a pinned handle into the debuggee for the rest of its life, pinning the heap you were inspecting. An address is valid only for the current stop; a moving GC relocates objects on every resume, so re-read it after each stop rather than caching it across a continue.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: write_memory
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Write up to 65536 base64-encoded bytes to the selected debug process. Get a managed object's address from the `address`/`address_length` fields on evaluate, get_members and get_frame values, as described on read_memory. The address is checked against nothing here: it is valid only for the stop it was read at, and writing through one cached across a continue corrupts whatever the GC moved into that space. Re-read it after every stop, and stay inside address_length.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_registers
tools.description: Return a stopped x64 thread's integer and control registers for CorDebug or Mono soft-debugger protocol 2.3+. Each row includes name, unsigned numeric value, fixed-width hexadecimal text, and bit width. The selected thread must be paused. READ frame_relation BEFORE THE NUMBERS. This is the OS thread's context, which at a managed stop is usually NOT the managed frame's: the runtime suspends the thread inside its own stop machinery, so rip sits in ntdll, rcx holds a wait handle rather than `this`, and rbp is a sentinel rather than a frame base. Those are true readings of the machine and wrong answers about the frame, and nothing in the values themselves tells them apart. frame_relation is "matched" (rip is inside this frame's JIT-compiled body, so the context does describe it), "unrelated" (it does not — the usual result at a breakpoint, and always so for any frame_index above 0, since rip belongs to the leaf), or "unknown" (the frame's native range could not be read). `note` says why. When it is not "matched", do not derive frame state from these registers: use get_frame, evaluate, or a value's `address` instead.

tools.name: get_members
tools.description: Expand one object one level, paged. Pass a returned member's `expression` back here to go deeper: depth is deliberately the caller's to control, because recursing server-side is unbounded on a cyclic object graph. A member whose `expression` is empty cannot be addressed at all: either a compiler-generated member (auto-property backing field, async or iterator state machine field, lambda display class) whose name is not spellable in any language, or a grouping row such as `Static members` that carries a type name rather than an expression. Its name, type and value are still accurate; do not retry it. Static members stay reachable by naming them directly, eg. `Some.Type.SomeStaticField`, but expression compilation still uses the selected frame's module; after CS0103 use get_callstack and select the nearest frame in the target module. Reports total and truncated. Members carry `address`/`address_length` when the runtime has one — see read_memory.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: set_value
tools.description: Assign to a local, parameter, field or property in the paused target. Always side-effecting: the assignment executes in the target. When this assignment prepares a flag, input, or counter that makes the target call the next method, keep the target paused for the assignment and then use run_to_method or run_to_location; do not manually assemble breakpoint, continue, wait, and cleanup. compiler_error=true means the expression did not compile and nothing ran; an error without it means the target may already have been touched. Executing in the target is not the same as needing a func-eval, and the difference decides what is still possible against an idle process. Storing a value that already exists over there is a direct write and succeeds even with every thread at an unsafe point; producing a value the engine must first create — a string literal, a boxed value, a new object — is a func-eval and is refused at an unsafe point like any other. The cost of the value is what matters, not whether the target is a primitive: assigning null to a reference is as free as assigning an int, while assigning a string literal to that same reference is refused. When it is refused, see invoke_method for how to reach a thread that can evaluate; note also that the unsafe-point thread's evaluable frame is often not frame 0, so pass frame_index for the frame whose locals you actually want. A CS0103 "does not exist in the current context" error names the variables this frame can actually address: when the engine recovers no source-level names for a method its locals are reachable only as the raw slots V_0, V_1, ..., which assign like any other name.

tools.name: search
tools.description: START HERE when you have a name and need a symbol. dnSpy's Search window as a tool: it matches the same candidate strings the GUI does, so a qualified path works — pattern 'GameState.ChatSystem' finds the ChatSystem field on type GameState, which search_symbols cannot. Space-separated terms are AND-ed, /slashes/ make it a regular expression, and kinds covers every entry of the GUI's Search For dropdown including property, event, parameter, local and literal. Every returned identifier round-trips: full_name is accepted back here as pattern, declaring_type is accepted by list_members and get_csharp, and module plus token is accepted by get_il, find_references and set_il_breakpoint. Nothing needs parsing. Bounded by max_scan over inspected symbols, not by the clock; scan_truncated=true means work stopped early and next_scan_offset resumes exactly where it left off. Pass module on Unity, where a whole-process scan means hundreds of thousands of framework symbols.

tools.description: Return up to 200 C# expressions referenced by the selected frame's current source statement. dgSpy derives the statement from dnSpy language debug info, maps its IL operands to active locals, parameters, this, and fields, then evaluates them through the normal value pipeline. host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_output
tools.description: Read the bounded non-destructive TEXT stream after a cursor: the debugged program's text plus the host's commentary, interleaved in one ring and told apart by category. DebugOutput is a managed debugger log message (for example Debugger.Log on CorDebug) and is available for attached as well as launched targets. StandardOutput and StandardError are a launched program's redirected stdout/stderr, reassembled into whole lines. Output, ErrorUser and StepFilter are host records, including the audit line every side-effecting call writes. An attached process's console handles were never ours, so its stdout/stderr cannot be captured after the fact. To block until the next line arrives instead of polling, use wait_for_output. Structured events — breakpoint hits, steps, exceptions, process exit — are not here; they are get_events.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

after_output_id.description: Cursor from a previous response's last_output_id. Omit to read from the oldest retained line.

tools.name: wait_for_output
tools.description: Wait, without consuming, for new text on exactly the stream get_output returns — debug output, launched-program stdout/stderr, and host commentary. Use it to wait for something the program writes; use wait_for_stop or wait_for_event to wait for a debugger event. A trailing line written without a newline is published after a short quiet period rather than held until its next write, so a prompt still arrives.

Pass category and name to read ONE entry, which is how a remove_exception_policy is confirmed: entries is empty and total is 0 when it is gone. Reports total and truncated.

tools.name: analyze_symbol
tools.description: Drill-in tool for a symbol `search` already found; it takes the module and token search returns. Return bounded typed caller, callee, construction, field, override, implementation, and attribute edges. Bounded by max_scan over inspected symbols and resumable: scan_truncated=true means work stopped early, and next_scan_offset fed back as scan_offset continues exactly there, so a module bigger than one call's bound is still coverable. Before the cursor existed, the callers of a method in a 7227-method module could not be found at any setting. Pass search_module on Unity, where an unfiltered scan means every framework assembly.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module_id.description: Opaque exact identity returned by list_modules, search, frames, and symbol results. It is scoped to one debugger session; refresh discovery after stale_module_id.

module.description: Legacy name/path selector; module_id is exact and preferred.

search_module.description: Filter on module name or path, by the same rule the module argument uses: exact name, name without its extension, or substring. Case-insensitive.

max_scan.description: Hard work bound in inspected symbols, types and methods alike; default 20000.

scan_offset.description: Resume cursor: pass a previous response's next_scan_offset, with the same search_module.

max_methods.description: The older name for max_scan, still honoured. Its old 5000 ceiling is gone; it was low enough to make large modules unreachable.
